newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., OKs $70 mln loan for team.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., OKs $70 mln loan for team.

text.p: The Sacramento City Council approved a plan on Wednesday to provide the Sacramento Kings with a $70 million loan to keep the basketball team playing in the city.
The council approved the proposal by a vote of 5-to-3 at a late night meeting.
After the vote, the mayor's spokesman said the loan was a good deal for the city and the team.
"There's no threat to the (city's) general fund. This is a very secure loan," said Michael Picker, Mayor Joe Serna Jr.'s chief of staff.
Under the plan, the city would issue up to $87.9 million of debt to provide the National Basketball Association Kings with the 30-year loan for $70 million.
The $87.9 million would include about $73 million of certificates of participation and about $15 million of revenue anticipation notes, Bill Farley, the city's economic development manager, said.
The Sacramento Kings will use the loan to retire debt. The deal calls for the Kings to pay the city the annual debt service each year from arena revenues and ticket surcharges.
The $87.9 million of debt would be secured by the full faith and credit of the city.
Sacramento's general fund would be protected by $120 million in loan collateral, including a $20 million note secured on the Kings' franchise, officials said.
Sacramento officials said they do not expect the financing to affect the city's credit ratings.

Kings owner Jim Thomas had originally proposed a $235 million public-private partnership with the city of Sacramento to develop a sports and entertainment complex. The proposal included $90 million to retire his existing debts.
The $235 million proposal, however, came under fire, and was withdrawn by Thomas in late January.
The final loan plan was unveiled in detail on Monday.
Without a financial commitment from Sacramento, Thomas had warned he might be forced to move the team to another city.
